title: Select: choosing and cancelling
purpose: Check that the Select field keeps your chosen value when its menu is cancelled, shows the current choice clearly, and stays usable with long option names. If you have a keyboard, also check type-ahead and opening keys.
changes: The selected value is separate from the highlighted option. The menu marks the current choice with a checkmark and returns to it when reopened. Long text stops before the arrow. Typing option names can select them while the field has focus.
steps: Tap the Power profile field and choose Performance. Check that the closed field displays Performance.
Open the menu again. Check that Performance has a checkmark. Tap empty space inside the example, outside the menu; the field should still display Performance.
Enable Long option labels. Open and close the field and check that long text never covers its arrow.

Optional keyboard check: focus the field and type b. It should choose a matching option without opening the menu. Arrow Down opens on the current choice; Arrow Up or Home opens on the first option; End opens on the last.
Optional keyboard check: navigate the open menu with arrows and press Escape. The prior choice must remain. Navigate again and press Enter to confirm the highlighted option.
Choose OK if the tested behavior is correct. Otherwise explain the problem below and choose Reject. Mention which step failed and what you saw.
expected: Choosing an option commits it; browsing and cancelling never commit another option. The current choice has a checkmark and is focused when the menu reopens. Long labels leave the arrow visible and clickable. Keyboard type-ahead and opening keys follow the stated behavior.
limits: This reviews the stated Select behavior and narrow-screen text layout. It does not establish complete Android pixel or motion parity, every filled/outlined variant, IME composition, or full localization support. Keyboard-only steps may be skipped on a phone without a keyboard.
